gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Soundcore Liberty 4 NC's factory firmware has no LDAC, so LDAC only appears after a firmware update started from the soundcore app, and that enabling it makes the buds leave multipoint. The same results also don't say that the EarFun Air Pro 4 keeps multipoint only on aptX Adaptive or Lossless, while two named reviewers report that the Air Pro 4+ keeps LDAC on with multipoint.
standout_why: I opened three rival pages. SoundGuys 'Best LDAC headphones and earbuds' (cited in two chats) already says 'you cannot use LDAC with Bluetooth multipoint' and that most Android phones default to 660 kbps in Best Effort mode. That is a general rule that names no product, and ChatGPT repeated it as a blanket statement in two answers. SoundGuys 'best wireless earbuds under $100' (cited in every chat) has none of these mechanics. It only says each model has LDAC 'for compatible Android phones'. Skimwire only says that aptX Lossless needs a Snapdragon Sound phone. None of the three says that the Liberty 4 NC ships without LDAC and needs an app-triggered firmware update. None says that Samsung phones may need a manual LDAC switch, or that the Air Pro 4+ appears to break the general rule. The GamesRadar Air Pro 4 review (cited) came back truncated, so I could not check it.
decides: For a shopper who wants LDAC on a phone and also multipoint with a laptop, these findings separate the candidates. The Liberty 4 NC (ChatGPT's 'best ANC' pick) and the Air Pro 4 both drop multipoint once LDAC is on. On the Air Pro 4, aptX Lossless or Adaptive keeps multipoint, but only on Snapdragon Sound phones, so Pixel and Exynos Galaxy owners can't take that route. Two named reviewers report that the Air Pro 4+ keeps LDAC with multipoint, which would make it the pick for that shopper. Our current page says '2 devices (not with LDAC)' for the 4+, and that cell needs rechecking before publishing. A Liberty 4 NC buyer must also run the in-app firmware update, or the buds have no LDAC at all.
